description: Rewrite the example app on preact, @preact/signals and htm. The example is 15 lines of imperative DOM left over from when it had to build the alt and crop modals itself; the component owns those now. Replace it with a preact app that renders the component and a live state panel driven by signals. Detailed spec and rationale live in specs/tasks/example-preact.md; read it before starting, especially the five preact-and-custom-element contract rules. Scope is example/ only -- no change to src/, the build scripts, or package.json. preact, @preact/signals and htm are already installed at compatible versions.

userStories.title: Preact renders the example, component included
userStories.description: As a developer reading the demo, I want the example written the way a real preact consumer would write it, so it shows me how to embed the component in a preact app.
acceptanceCriteria:
example/index.html gains a
alongside the existing module script tag
example/index.ts defines an App component using html from htm/preact and mounts it with preact's render into #app
App renders the <image-input> element itself, with static attributes only and no dynamic props
The <image-input> vnode has a stable position in the tree and carries no key attribute
import '../src/index.js' stays above the render() call, so preact only ever sees an upgraded element
The imperative document.body.innerHTML += markup string is gone
npm run build-example succeeds and npx eslint example/*.ts passes with no config change
npm test still passes end to end
userStories.notes: No dynamic props is a correctness rule, not style: the component owns alt as a reflected attribute written from inside by handleChange_alt, so a preact-driven alt prop would put two writers on one attribute. Preact 10 sets a property when `name in domElement` and an attribute otherwise, which is why the import must stay above render() -- an un-upgraded element silently takes the attribute path. Recreating the <image-input> DOM node would destroy its file, object URL, preview and both dialogs, which is why no key.

userStories.title: Signals hold the demo state and a panel displays it
userStories.description: As a developer reading the demo, I want to see the component's state rendered on the page, so I can tell what the component exposes without opening devtools.
acceptanceCriteria: New file example/state.ts exports five signals: altText, fileName, fileSize, lastEvent, errorReason
New file example/panel.ts exports a Panel component that displays all five
App renders Panel as a sibling of the <image-input>
Signals are read only inside Panel, never inside App
Text-only signals are passed straight into text position so @preact/signals binds a text node rather than re-rendering
npm run build-example succeeds and npx eslint example/*.ts passes with no config change
npm test still passes end to end
userStories.notes: A signal read inside App would subscribe App, so every event would re-render the tree containing the <image-input> vnode. That is harmless given EP-001's static-props rule, but reading signals as deep as possible keeps it harmless by construction instead of by accident. At this point the panel shows initial empty values; EP-003 makes it live.

userStories.title: Listeners keep the panel current
userStories.description: As a developer trying the demo, I want the panel to update as I pick, crop, describe and remove an image, so I can watch the component's events as they fire.
acceptanceCriteria: App takes a ref to the <image-input> and attaches its listeners in a useEffect
The effect returns a cleanup that removes every listener it added
Listeners are attached with addEventListener via the ref, NOT with preact on* props

image-input:change sets fileName, fileSize and lastEvent and clears errorReason; image-input:alt-change sets altText and lastEvent; image-input:remove clears fileName and fileSize and sets lastEvent; image-input:error sets errorReason and lastEvent

The remove handler does NOT clear altText, because the component's #clear() ends with `this.alt = null` (src/index.ts:318), which emits image-input:alt-change with an empty string and so clears it through the alt-change handler already
image-input:edit and image-input:alt each set lastEvent, so the panel shows they still fire even though the component opens its own dialogs
Every handler that sets more than one signal wraps them in batch from @preact/signals
npm run build-example succeeds and npx eslint example/*.ts passes with no config change
npm test still passes end to end
userStories.notes: Preact lowercases event prop names and a colon cannot survive as a prop name, so there is no onImage-input:change to write -- the ref plus useEffect is the only workable route, not a stylistic preference. The batch requirement comes from the repo's frontend state rule in CLAUDE.md.

userStories.title: The example's AGENTS.md records the preact contract
userStories.description: As the next agent to touch the example, I want the preact and custom-element rules written down, so I do not undo them by accident.
acceptanceCriteria: example/AGENTS.md documents all five contract rules: no dynamic props on the component, import before render, listeners via ref and useEffect rather than on* props, stable position and no key, and signals read in Panel rather than App
Each rule records WHY, not just what, so a reader can tell which are correctness rules and which are convention
The note about example/index.css being demo-only styling is preserved
No em dashes and no arrow characters anywhere in the file
npm test still passes end to end
userStories.notes: Do not write tests for documentation. example/AGENTS.md was already rewritten once when the component took over the dialogs -- it previously claimed the components were headless with respect to dialogs, which had become false. Check its current contents before editing rather than assuming.
